arguments.name: Preservation to personal survival
arguments.position: Conditional project argument skeleton; not a finding
premises: A foundation retains information about a deceased individual (H-P-information).
bridge_principles: B05: the retention relation preserves the numerically same subject, not merely a representation.
An explicit identity theory establishes subjectivity beyond the bodily-life boundary.
arguments.conclusion: If both additional premises hold, H-S follows for the specified person.
arguments.strongest_objection: Information preservation can occur while the original subject ceases; duplicates expose the identity problem.
arguments.strongest_reply: Specify a subject-preserving relation rather than infer it from informational fidelity.
unresolved_issues: The identity relation and first-person continuation remain unresolved.

arguments.name: Endurance and enduring significance
arguments.position: Conditional project argument skeleton; not a finding
premises: A specified person or item persists under H-S or H-P.
bridge_principles: B09: persistence of that subject or item is valuable under a stated normative account.
B09: the proposed value is not defeated by the content or conditions of persistence.
arguments.conclusion: The specified persistence contributes enduring significance under those normative premises.
arguments.strongest_objection: Duration alone need not increase value, and finite value may exist without persistence.
arguments.strongest_reply: Identify the particular value preserved, such as a relationship, and argue for its normative importance.
unresolved_issues: Whether endurance is necessary, sufficient, or merely contributory must be assessed separately.
Neither objective value nor cosmic purpose follows from duration alone.

arguments.name: Conscious production to cosmic purpose
arguments.position: Conditional project argument skeleton; not a finding
premises: Conscious experience occurs within the universe, treated here as an assumed explanandum without empirical assessment.
bridge_principles: B08: an agent independently specified that outcome as an end and grounds or directs the universe toward it.
arguments.conclusion: H-I holds for that specified end if the agency and intention premises are warranted.
arguments.strongest_objection: The occurrence of an outcome is also compatible with an unintended byproduct.
arguments.strongest_reply: State ends and discriminating consequences independently of the observations being explained.
unresolved_issues: No evidence for an intending agent has been assessed.
Goodness, authority, survival and preservation remain separate.

arguments.name: Conscious foundation to moral authority
arguments.position: Conditional project argument skeleton; not a finding
premises: A proposed foundation exists and stands in specified creative or unifying relations to individuals (assumed for argument only).
bridge_principles: B10-B12: a stated normative principle connects those relations or a specified good nature to genuine reasons and obligations.
The normative principle explains binding force without identifying goodness merely with whatever the foundation does.
arguments.conclusion: H-A follows only to the extent the normative relation establishes the specified obligations.
arguments.strongest_objection: Descriptive unity, causal origin, power, or reward can leave binding moral justification unexplained.
arguments.strongest_reply: Develop a defensible good-nature or relational grounding account and compare non-theistic value/reason/obligation accounts.
unresolved_issues: Existence and goodness of the foundation are unassessed.
Objective value, moral reasons and obligations require separately explicit grounding.
Accountability and motivation do not settle authority.
